title: Prawn Cocktail
subtitle: Classic British starter with Marie Rose sauce
excerpt: Chilled cooked prawns in a tangy Marie Rose sauce served on crisp iceberg lettuce with a wedge of lemon. The British starter that never really went out of style.

recipe.sourceNotes: Prawn cocktail was the defining British restaurant starter from the 1960s through to the 1980s, appearing on virtually every gastropub and hotel menu. It was introduced to Britain from America, where shrimp cocktail had been popular since the 1950s. The Marie Rose sauce (a blend of mayonnaise and ketchup with Worcestershire sauce and lemon) was popularised in Britain by chef Fanny Cradock. The combination fell out of fashion as food trends moved on and was mocked as dated for several decades, before being reassessed and restored to menus from the 2000s onwards. When made with good prawns and a properly seasoned sauce, it remains an excellent starter. Use the best prawns you can find: large North Atlantic prawns have better flavour than small tropical prawns.

content.text: The sauce must be well seasoned. Taste it before assembling: it should be tangy, slightly sweet, and have a distinct kick from the Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco. The prawns and sauce can be combined up to an hour before serving and kept in the fridge. Do not assemble the glasses until the last minute or the lettuce will wilt.

items.preparation: half for the sauce, half cut into wedges to serve

content.text: Make the Marie Rose sauce: mix together the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, cayenne, and salt. Taste and adjust: it should be tangy and well seasoned.
Fold the prawns gently into the sauce, reserving 4 large prawns per person to drape over the edge of the glass.

Arrange the shredded lettuce in the base of 4 glasses or ramekins. Spoon the prawn mixture over. Drape the reserved prawns over the edge. Dust with smoked paprika. Serve with a wedge of lemon and brown bread and butter.
